subject.title: Session files not being cleaned up (disk bloat)

question: Should this issue remain the umbrella for `.bak.*`, stale `.tmp`, checkpoint/orphan, and proactive cleanup semantics after the deleted/reset reporting PR, or should maintainers split those remaining artifact classes into narrower follow-up issues?
rationale: Current main and the open PR only cover part of the report, while deleting `.bak.*` and running proactive cleanup changes recovery and retention behavior that automation should not decide alone.

options.title: Keep umbrella and define policy
options.body: Use this issue to settle the remaining artifact classes and then implement one consistent cleanup policy after the narrower PR is reviewed.

options.title: Split into focused follow-ups
options.body: Keep the deleted/reset cleanup issue and PR as the immediate path, then open narrower issues for `.bak.*` retention and proactive stale-temp cleanup.

options.title: Document manual cleanup only
options.body: Accept current runtime behavior and clarify that `.bak.*` and some stale artifacts are only removed by explicit cleanup or disk-budget pressure.

recommendation.title: Keep umbrella and define policy
recommendation.body: Use this issue to settle the remaining artifact classes and then implement one consistent cleanup policy after the narrower PR is reviewed.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the relevant session maintenance controls and cleanup UX, making them the strongest available owner for the policy shape.
